Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test case "testIndexOfAnyBut_StringStringWithSupplementaryChars" attempts to verify that the method StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(String, String) correctly handles Unicode supplementary characters (characters outside the basic multilingual plane that are represented by surrogate pairs in Java strings).

The test uses two supplementary characters: CharU20000 (U+20000) and CharU20001 (U+20001). These are represented as surrogate pairs ("\uD840\uDC00" and "\uD840\uDC01") in Java strings.

The bug report summary indicates that StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly; specifically the containsAny and related methods.

Looking at the implementation of StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut:
- It first checks for empty input strings and returns INDEX_NOT_FOUND (-1).
- Then it iterates over each character of the input string with a for-loop from i=0 to strLen-1.
- On each iteration, it extracts the character at position i using str.charAt(i), which returns a char (value 16 bits).
- It then calls searchChars.indexOf(ch) to check if this single char is present in searchChars.
- If not found, it returns the current index i.

The problem is that this iteration and character checking is operating at the "char" level, not code point level. For supplementary characters, which are stored as surrogate pairs (two chars), this will split a single supplementary character into two separate char values. Therefore, this method will not properly match supplementary characters, as it treats surrogate halves individually.

The test case expects the index of the first character in the string that is not one of the supplementary characters specified. However, because the implementation is looking at individual chars, it will not correctly identify surrogate pairs as single characters and may give incorrect result or fail.

In summary, the root cause of the bug is that StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut operates on single 16-bit char units instead of code points, causing it to mishandle supplementary Unicode characters represented by surrogate pairs.

Thus, StringUtils methods that use similar logic need to be updated to operate at the code point level to correctly handle supplementary characters.

Next, I will check if there is a similar method for iterating over code points or use codePointAt instead of charAt.

- The test testIndexOfAnyBut_StringStringWithSupplementaryChars tries to verify the handling of supplementary Unicode characters (like U+20000) by StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut.
- Supplementary characters in Java are encoded as surrogate pairs (two char values).
- The method StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(String, String) iterates the input string by charAt(i), which gives only 16-bit char units, not full Unicode codepoints.
- It compares each single char with searchChars using indexOf(char), so it does not treat surrogate pairs properly as one character.
- Therefore, indexOfAnyBut fails to correctly find or exclude supplementary characters, causing the test failure.
- The root cause is that the implementation works at the char level instead of the codepoint level and hence does not support Unicode supplementary characters.
- The test fails as it relies on correct handling of these supplementary characters represented by surrogate pairs.

Recommended fix is to update this method and others in StringUtils to use codePointAt and related codepoint-aware iteration instead of charAt, to handle supplementary Unicode properly.
